title: Write a function that adds two values
prompt: Write add(a, b). Return their sum. Inputs and their sum are in the int range. Return the value; the supplied driver prints it.
solution:
#include <iostream>

int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
driver: int main(){ int a,b; if(!(std::cin>>a>>b)) return 2; std::cout<<add(a,b)<<"\n"; }

tests.label: Two positive values
tests.hint: Use both parameters in the returned expression.

tests.label: Negative and positive
tests.hint: Addition must keep the sign of the result.

tests.label: Both negative
tests.hint: Do not replace addition with an absolute value.

hints: A return statement sends a value back to the caller.
explanation: return a + b computes and returns one int. The driver owns input and output, so the function can be tested without reading a terminal.
